newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Sth Australia signs hardwood deal with Japan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Sth Australia signs hardwood deal with Japan.

text.p: The South Australian Government said on Wednesday it had signed a deal with three Japanese buyers to secure both markets and prices for hardwood produced in the Green Triangle region of south-eastern Australia.

Primary Industry Minister Rob Kerin said the agreement with Nippon Paper Treefarm Australia, Mitsui & Co's Mitsui Plantation Development, and MCA Afforestation would result in millions of trees planted in SA's south-west and western Victoria.
The Blue Gum (Eucalyptus globulus) trees grown under this project would be chipped and exported to Japan for use by paper manufacturer Nippon Paper Industries, he said in a statement.
The project aimed to establish 1000 hectares of Blue Gums annually with a rotation of about 10-12 years, he said.
He did not give any details on the value of the agreement.
Kerin also said that following a review, the government has reaffirmed it would not sell off its 60,000 hectares of forests in the State's south-east nor their harvesting rights.
It would aim to double the rate of annual new plantation establishment to at least 1,500 hectares.
